title: ZeRO-3 CPU offload set_local_grad does not refresh norm_for_param_grads — gradient clipping uses pre-clipping norm
trigger_conditions: user calls safe_set_local_grad to modify a partition's gradient between backward and step (e.g. external clipping/sanitizing)
root_cause: set_local_grad copies the supplied tensor into the fp32 partition's grad slot but does not update self.norm_for_param_grads[param_id]. With CPU offload, scaled_global_grad_norm is later computed as the L2-aggregate of these cached per-param norms (because the actual grad lives in pinned CPU memory). The aggregate therefore reflects pre-modification gradients, while unscale_and_clip_grads applies a clip factor based on this stale norm to the modified grads — silent mis-clipping. Note that scaled_global_grad_norm also drives the loss-scale-aware clip decision in optimizer.step.
invariant: Whenever fp32 grad partition for param p is overwritten via set_local_grad, norm_for_param_grads[p] must equal _constant_buffered_norm2 of the new gradient.
diff_summary: In _set_fp32_grad_state_partition (CPU offload branch), update self.norm_for_param_grads[param_id] = self._constant_buffered_norm2(value).
silent_check: All updates write valid finite tensors. The clipping decision is just based on a stale (typically larger) norm, so clip factor is wrong but always finite — optimizer.step proceeds, no exception.
